To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel bodily illusion elicited by tendon vibration of the right hand during bimanual interaction of the hands with a cylinder activates anterior parts of the right and left superior parietal lobe bilaterally.
the "bimanual illusion of hand flexion and shrinking of a hand-held object" activates the anterior part of the superior pariental lobule bilaterally.

a bodily illusion elicited by tendon vibration of the wrist extensor muscle activates bilateral anterior parts of the SPL and that this region has never been reported to be activated in previous studies of unimanual hand and hand-object illusions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of bimanual hand-object illusion and the spatial relationship between two hands and an external object.
the neural correlates of bimanual interactions with external objects.
the somatic perception in bimanual interaction, which is an important issue for understanding human social behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anterior SPL is activated when the spatial relationship between two hands and a held object changes.

the anterior SPL is involved in the somato-sensory perception of the bimanual interaction of the hands with an external object, and that this perception may be based on a spatial representation of the two hands and the object.
the anterior SPL plays a key role in the somatic representation of the spatial relationship between one's own body and external object.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain represents the relationship between one's own body and an external object by integrating the information of the two hands, the hand-held object and the spatial relationship between them.
the anterior SPL is involved in the spatial computation of the own body in relation to an external object.

a somatic illusion of the right hand flexing and a hand-held cylinder shrinking from the right is associated with activation of the left-hemispherical hand area 2 and left inferior parietal cortex and bilateral SPL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain represents bimanual interaction in the SPL.
the human SPL is involved in somatosensory perception of the spatial relationship between two hands and a grasped object.
a novel bodily illusion was created in conjunction with fMRI, and the results suggest the existence of a neural mechanism for the somatic perception in bimanual interaction.
